Subject: Acceptance gates, instrumentation & user-scenario runbook

Hi Sam / Grace —

Following our demo last week, attached is a first draft of the MAP and a focused smoke-test runbook that maps directly to acceptance gates. Goal: align on the exact pass/fail checks we need during the 2-week evaluation and confirm the close criteria so procurement can schedule contract steps.

Attachments:
- Convergent_MAP_v1.xlsx (outline of milestones, owners, dates)
- convergent_smoke_test_plan.md (step-by-step verification & sample requests)

High-level ask: can you review the acceptance gates below and confirm any gaps by EOD Friday (Jan 23)? If we get sign-off, we’ll lock the evaluation window Jan 26–Feb 6 and run the smoke suite on day 1 and day 7.

Proposed acceptance gates (short):
1) Functional correctness: 90% top-line intent precision on the 200-case user-scenario set (see sheet: "User Scenarios").
2) Latency SLO: p95 response latency < 600ms for interactive workflows during controlled load (1 request/sec per seat).
3) Stability: error rate < 0.5% under sustained baseline traffic (72-hour sample).
4) Data controls: VPC/private routing verified; logs and audit events captured for tokens 1–N (per instrumentation checklist).
5) Safety/concordance: no high-severity hallucinations on 100 safety probe queries (defined list).

Exit gates (hard stop conditions):
- Persistent p95 > 1200ms across two consecutive run windows.
- Failed safety probes > 5% (high severity).
- Inability to enable required audit logging or KMS integration within the evaluation window.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- User-scenario runs: 200 seeded prompts, concordance measured against gold answers; pass if >= 90% exact/near-exact matches.
- Load trial: controlled burst to 2x baseline to validate autoscaling and latency profile.
- Trace verification: distributed trace present for 100% of requests in the smoke run; token-level timing present for sample requests.

Instrumentation required from your side (minimum):
- Endpoint ACLs to permit Redwood test agents by Jan 25.
- Access to a small synthetic dataset for the seeded user scenarios (sheet in the MAP).
- A short-lived service account (read-only) to validate audit logs.

Owners & timeline (draft):
- Camila (RED) — MAP owner, coordinates runbook & evidence collection.
- Karthik (RED) — performance & latency signoffs, runs load trials.
- Laura (RED) — acceptance evidence packaging for procurement.
- Sam (Convergent) — test data, procurement point-of-contact.

Next steps:
1) Sam/Grace confirm gaps by EOD Jan 23.
2) Lock evaluation window and schedule kickoff session Jan 25 (30m).
3) Smoke test run day 1 (Jan 26) and day 7; final acceptance report by Feb 9.

Thanks — happy to walk through the MAP live if useful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Camila —

Thanks for the draft. A few quick clarifications before our team can sign off:
1) The latency SLO: is the 600ms p95 including network egress back to our app, or just the inference window on your dedicated instance? We need to map to our client-observed latency.
2) For the 200-case user-scenario set, can you share a small sample (10 cases) so our clinical reviewers can eyeball the gold answers first?
3) On "audit logs captured for tokens 1–N" — we need to verify token-level logging is compatible with our PII scrub policy. Can you point to the exact log fields and retention policy?

Also: we have a compliance checkpoint on Feb 2 — if we don't have KMS integration by then we'll need to delay moving to prod. That sounds like one of your exit gates but want to flag it.

On Fri, Jan 23, 2026 at 11:06 AM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com> wrote:

> Sam — great questions, thanks. Answers inline and updated plan below.
>
> 1) Latency SLO: the map uses Redwood-measured inference latency (server-side). We’ll provide an estimated client-observed latency delta (network + app instrumentation) during the first smoke run. If you prefer the SLO to be client-observed, we can update but it will require a short sidecar measurement on your app.
>
> 2) Sample scenarios: attached 10-sample prompts in sheet 'Sample10' (MAP). I pulled examples that map to the clinical paths you showed in the demo.
>
> 3) Audit logs / PII: Redwood audit events include request_id, timestamp, model_version, decision_flags, and a hashed user_id by default. Plaintext user payloads are not retained in audit logs unless you enable full request capture (we don't enable by default). Retention is configurable; for the evaluation we suggest 30-day retention with read-only export to your S3 bucket.
>
> Updated acceptance checklist (condensed for quick review):
> - Acceptance A: Functional concordance >= 90% on seeded set (200) — owner: Convergent reviewers & RED verification.
> - Acceptance B: p95 client-observed latency < 700ms OR server p95 < 600ms + documented delta — owner: Karthik + Sam.
> - Acceptance C: Audit log delivery & KMS proof-of-concept: logs visible in your S3 + test key rotation event observed — owner: Laura + Sam.
> - Acceptance D: Safety probes: zero high-severity failures in 100-sample probes — owner: Convergent safety lead + RED.
>
> Smoke test steps (day 1):
> - Run 30 representative user-scenarios (subset of 200) — verify output & log capture.
> - Execute 10 safety probes.
> - Run single-node burst (10 concurrent requests) and capture p95.
> - Validate audit events in S3 (sample export).
>
> Rollback triggers (immediate stop & triage):
> - Any safety probe with high-severity failure.
> - p95 > 1200ms in two consecutive burst windows.
> - Inability to produce audit logs or access KMS logs within 24 hours of request.
>
> Evidence deliverables post-eval: smoke-run logs, concordance scoring sheet (CSV), latency distributions, and a short video of the end-to-end flow for procurement.
>
> I attached the updated MAP (v1.1) with the sample10 sheet and a checklist column for signatures. If that aligns, can we schedule Jan 25 9:00 AM PT for a 30-minute kickoff?
>
> Cheers,
> Camila
